subject: Mayor Lungo-Koehn on City Development and Schools
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn regarding city administration achievements, infrastructure projects, and strategic planning for housing and education.

items.title: Mayor's Background and Philosophy
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn shared personal details about her family life, coaching experience, and her commitment to ethical decision-making in city government.

items.title: City Accomplishments
items.summary: The Mayor highlighted improvements to city hiring practices, park renovations, expanded social services through recovery coaches, and millions of dollars in fire station updates.

items.title: Current Challenges and Affordability
items.summary: Discussion addressed resident concerns regarding food insecurity, rising costs for heating and housing, and the difficulties of managing city personnel matters.

items.title: Public Communication and Engagement
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn outlined the city's multi-channel communication approach, including newsletters, robocalls, and the launch of a new neighborhood liaison committee.

items.title: Zoning and Housing Strategy
items.summary: The Mayor explained the decision to slow the zoning process to allow for better transparency and discussed balancing new development with parking needs in Medford Square.

items.title: Medford High School Project
items.summary: The Mayor discussed the deteriorating state of the high school and the need to find a sustainable budget for a new facility that can pass a future debt exclusion vote.

items.title: Future Vision for Medford
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn envisioned a 2050 Medford featuring a vibrant Medford Square with a grocery store, mixed-use housing, and modernized athletic fields.
